lesson:prompt.capital_of__note: Question prompt. {entityName} is a localised country name from the content pack.
lesson:prompt.locate__note: Map question prompt. {entityName} is a localised name from the content pack.
lesson:feedback.correct.title: Perfect!
lesson:feedback.correct.title__note: Celebration headline after a correct answer. One word, one exclamation mark maximum.
lesson:feedback.correct.body__note: Shown under the celebration headline. {entityName} is a localised name.
lesson:feedback.correct.streak__note: Replaces feedback.correct.body once the user has answered three or more in a row correctly. Only ever shown when that is actually true — claiming a roll after one right answer is flattery, and this app states the truth.
lesson:feedback.wrong.title: That's {chosen}.
lesson:feedback.wrong.title__note: NEVER 'Wrong!' or 'Oops!'. State the truth plainly — no exclamation mark, no sad emoji. See docs/design/voice-and-tone.md.
lesson:feedback.wrong.body__note: Used ONLY when a hint exists (flag descriptions). Names the right answer and gives one memorable hook.
lesson:leave.confirm: Leave lesson? Your progress is saved.
lesson:summary.perfect.title: Flawless.
lesson:summary.perfect.title__note: End-of-lesson headline when every answer was right. One word. Satisfied and closing — never urging another lesson.
lesson:summary.perfect.body: Every one right. That's not luck.
lesson:summary.perfect.body__note: Shown under the perfect-lesson headline. Credits the person, not chance.
lesson:summary.strong.title: Nice work.
lesson:summary.strong.title__note: End-of-lesson headline at 80% accuracy or better. Satisfied and closing.
lesson:summary.strong.body: That's the world a little smaller.
lesson:summary.strong.body__note: The house line for a good lesson — see docs/design/voice-and-tone.md.
lesson:summary.done.title: Lesson complete.
lesson:summary.done.title__note: End-of-lesson headline below 80% accuracy, and after running out of hearts. States the fact. NEVER 'Keep practising' or anything implying the result fell short.
lesson:summary.done.body: The tricky ones are the ones that stick.
lesson:summary.done.body__note: The most important string on this screen: it is read by someone who just got several wrong, and it must be true rather than consoling. Harder recall really does produce stronger memory. No 'but', no 'don't worry'.
lesson:summary.early.title: Stopped there.
lesson:summary.early.title__note: Headline when the user chose to finish the lesson early. Matter-of-fact. Never 'You gave up' and never a celebration — this is not a completed lesson.
lesson:summary.early.body: Everything you answered counts. Come back whenever.
lesson:summary.early.body__note: Reassures that leaving early loses nothing, because it does not — every answer is submitted. Ends on the open door.
lesson:summary.none.body: No answers to count this time. The lesson will be waiting.
lesson:summary.none.body__note: Shown when the lesson ended before a single answer, so there is nothing to total up. Never framed as a wasted trip.
lesson:summary.xpUnit__note: Unit label under the big XP number. Keep the abbreviation if it is used in the target language; expand only if 'XP' is meaningless there.
lesson:summary.stat.percent__note: Accuracy as a percentage. Some languages put a space before the percent sign — Swedish does.
lesson:summary.stat.accuracy__note: Label under the accuracy figure on the lesson summary. Max 14 characters — it sits in a narrow tile.
lesson:summary.stat.accuracy.a11y__note: Spoken label for the accuracy tile, so it is a full phrase. Leads with the count because 'seven of ten' is more useful than a percentage read aloud.
lesson:summary.stat.coins__note: Label under the coins figure on the lesson summary. Max 14 characters.
lesson:summary.stat.stronger__note: Label under the count of facts that moved up a mastery level. The product's actual promise, so it names learning rather than score. Max 14 characters.
lesson:summary.stat.stronger.a11y: {count, plural, =0 {No facts moved up a level this time} one {# fact moved up a level} other {# facts moved up a level}}
lesson:summary.stat.stronger.a11y__note: Spoken label for the 'facts stronger' tile. The zero case is neutral, never disappointed — reviewing something you already know is a normal lesson.
lesson:summary.practised__note: Heading over the row of flags for the countries in the lesson just finished. Deliberately places the user IN the world rather than reporting on a score. Max 22 characters.
lesson:hearts.empty.title: Out of hearts
lesson:hearts.empty.title__note: Headline when hearts run out. Neutral and factual, never a punishment.
lesson:hearts.empty.body: Hearts come back over time. Practice mode is always free.
lesson:hearts.empty.body__note: Critical: must make clear that learning is NEVER blocked.
lesson:hearts.out.title: That's the last heart
lesson:hearts.out.title__note: Heading when hearts run out mid-lesson. States the fact. Never 'You failed' or 'Game over' — the user has not failed, the lesson has ended early. Max 28 characters.
lesson:hearts.out.body: You keep everything you got right. The next lesson starts with a full set.
lesson:hearts.out.body__note: The single most important string in this state. Hearts reset per lesson, so this is never a lockout — but a child who has just been stopped does not know that. Must appear BEFORE any offer to spend coins. Never mention a refill timer: there is none, the next lesson simply starts fresh.
lesson:hearts.out.revive__note: Button to spend coins and finish the current lesson. {price} is a coin amount. Buys the moment, not access — the next lesson is free either way.
lesson:hearts.out.cantAfford: {short} coins short — but the next lesson is free anyway.
lesson:hearts.out.cantAfford__note: Shown instead of the continue button when the user cannot afford it. Ends on the reassurance rather than the gap, and never links to a store: coins come from lessons, never from money.
lesson:hearts.out.finish__note: Ends the lesson and goes to the summary, keeping every answer already given. Always present, and never framed as giving up. Max 16 characters.
lesson:close__note: Accessibility label for the close/pause control in the lesson header. Describes the ACTION, not the icon — it pauses rather than quitting, so a mis-tap is recoverable.
lesson:paused.title: Paused
lesson:paused.title__note: Heading on the pause overlay. One word. Never 'Are you sure?' — leaving is safe and the copy must not imply otherwise. Max 12 characters.
lesson:paused.body: Take your time. Nothing is lost.
lesson:paused.body__note: Shown when the user pauses before answering anything. Max 40 characters.
lesson:paused.kept: {count, plural, one {Your # answer is saved} other {Your # answers are saved}} — leaving now keeps them.
lesson:paused.kept__note: Shown when the user has answered at least one question. Names the count rather than saying 'your progress is safe', because a number can be checked and a reassurance cannot. NEVER warn about losing progress: abandoning keeps and submits every answer.
lesson:paused.resume__note: Primary action on the pause overlay — most taps of a close button want this. Max 16 characters.
lesson:paused.finish__note: Ends the lesson, keeping every answer given. Never framed as quitting or giving up. Max 16 characters.
lesson:progress.label: Progress
lesson:progress.label__note: Label above the lesson progress bar. Max 10 chars.
lesson:hearts.remaining: {count, plural, =0 {No hearts left} one {# heart left} other {# hearts left}}
lesson:hearts.remaining__note: Accessibility label for the hearts indicator. ICU plural.
lesson:reward.xp__note: Accessibility label for the XP chip. Spoken, so it is a full phrase.
lesson:reward.coins__note: Accessibility label for the coin chip.
lesson:empty.title: You're all caught up
lesson:empty.title__note: Shown when nothing is due. Celebrate it — never a dead end.
lesson:empty.body: Nothing is due right now. Explore somewhere new?
lesson:empty.body__note: Empty state body. Always offers the next step.
lesson:prompt.capital_reverse: {valueName} is the capital of which country?
lesson:prompt.capital_reverse__note: Reverse capital question. {valueName} is a city name.
lesson:prompt.flag_of: What does the flag of {entityName} look like?
lesson:prompt.flag_of__note: Reverse flag question — the answer is a description like "a red circle on a white field". {entityName} is a localised name from the content pack.
lesson:prompt.flag_described__note: Screen-reader-safe flag question. {description} is a phrase like "a red circle on a white field".
lesson:feedback.wrong.bodyPlain__note: Used when the fact carries no descriptive hint, e.g. a capital. Still states the answer plainly — never just "wrong".
lesson:prompt.currency_of: What money do people use in {entityName}?
lesson:prompt.currency_of__note: Currency question. Deliberately plain — 'What is the currency of X?' is a phrase a ten-year-old reads past. {entityName} is a localised country name.
lesson:prompt.currency_reverse__note: Reverse currency question. Only generated when the currency belongs to exactly one country — the engine refuses it for the euro.
lesson:speed.title: Speed round
lesson:speed.title__note: Name of the timed lesson mode.
lesson:speed.body: Ten questions, {seconds} seconds each. Missing one costs nothing.
lesson:speed.body__note: Explains the mode before it starts. The last sentence matters — it is what makes the mode playful rather than punishing.
lesson:speed.remaining__note: Accessibility label for the countdown. Read on demand, never announced every second.
lesson:speed.timeUp__note: Shown when a question times out. Neutral and brief — it is the clock's doing, not a failure. NEVER 'Too slow!'.
lesson:prompt.which_country_map__note: Map question — the locator map IS the prompt, with the country picked out against the land around it. "Highlighted" rather than "shown", because the map shows several countries and only one is coloured. Never shown to a screen-reader user; tpl.location-of.mc4 tests the same fact by ear.
lesson:prompt.location_of__note: The screen-reader-safe sibling of the map question, and a good question in its own right. Answers are subregions — "Northern Europe", "West Africa". {entityName} takes the sentence form, so English gets "the United States".
lesson:answer.correct__note: Accessibility label for the option that IS the answer, once feedback is showing. The tick beside it is `aria-hidden` artwork, so without this a screen-reader user hears only the option text and has no way to tell which one was right — colour and an unlabelled icon are the whole signal on screen.
lesson:answer.wrong__note: Accessibility label for the option the user chose when it was wrong. Deliberately NOT 'incorrect' or 'wrong answer' shouted at the user — it states which option is not the answer, in the same register as the visible copy 'That's Berlin. The answer is Paris.' See docs/design/voice-and-tone.md.
